newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia textile exports up but seen competitive.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia textile exports up but seen competitive.

text.p: Tunisia's 1996 textile exports rose 5.8 percent from 1995, but manufacturers said on Thursday tough challenges lay ahead for this key export earner as customs barriers fell in world markets.
Tunisia exported textiles worth 2.48 billion dinars ($2.3 billion) in 1996, up from 2.34 billion dinars in 1995, official statistics showed.
Raw material and textile imports for the sector rose 5.9 percent to 1.85 billion dinars from 1.74 million dinars in 1995.
In addition, capital goods imports for the sector were estimated near 100 million dinars yearly, professionals said.
The European Union (EU) took 94.2 percent of textile exports, consisting mostly of jeans and hosiery, due to generous quotas granted by Brussels.

But progressive dismantling of customs barriers as a result of a free trade accord signed with the EU last year and an expected influx of Asian competitors is worrying many businessmen here about future prospects.

The first challenge is the dismantling of the multi-fibres accord, started in 1995. The accord is speeding up competition from Asian countries, which were limited by quotas in the EU, industry sources said.

"Our worries are about the weaving and spinning firms, which were up to now, protected by customs barriers and are to face increasing competition with the opening up of Tunisia's trade exchanges," the professionals' head Mohsen Ben Abdallah told journalists on Thursday.
Thirty percent of more than 200 firms working for weaving and spinning are under threat of collapse, he said.
In 1996, Tunisia had 2,015 textile firms, with 1,277 having an offshore status and either owned by European investors outright or run as joint ventures with Tunisian partners.

A programme to adapt the textile industry to the new international environment started in 1996 with an estimated investment need of 700 million dinars over the next five years, mainly to renovate old equipment.
The sector employs 200,000 to 220,000 people, representing nearly half of the country's manufacturing labor force.

Ben Abdallah said a professional textile and cloting exhibit will be in Tunis on November 12-15. The exhibit will include for the first time, professionnals from Mediterranean countries Morocco, Algeria, Turkey, Italy, France, Germany and Belgium were invited, he said. ($ = 1.096 Tunisian Dinars)
